name: Donn Fírinne

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Donn Fírinne was an Irish fairy king. He ruled within Knockfierna mountain in County Limerick. The mountain is Cnoc Fírinne, the hill of Fírinne. Inside sat his fairy palace, the sídhe. He belonged to the fairy race, the Tuatha Dé Danann. He was one of the best-known fairy kings of Ireland. He sometimes kidnapped mortal women. The women joined his fairy dances. They never appeared in the surface world again. He may connect to Donn, the obscure king of the dead.
objective: Records Donn Fírinne, a Tuatha Dé Danann fairy king who ruled from a palace inside Knockfierna and kidnapped mortal women.
key_results: Donn Fírinne was a fairy king within Knockfierna mountain in County Limerick.
He belonged to the Tuatha Dé Danann, Ireland's magical race.
He was one of the best-known fairy kings of the land.
He sometimes kidnapped mortal women, who were never seen again on the surface.
He may be connected to Donn, the obscure king of the dead.
